newsitem.title: UK: OECD oil stocks fall 200,000 bpd in July - IEA.
newsitem.headline: OECD oil stocks fall 200,000 bpd in July - IEA.

text.p: Oil stocks held by industry in the OECD fell by 200,000 barrels per day (bpd) to stand 153 million barrels below the peak in 1995, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said in its monthly oil report.

"However, stock levels decreased sharply in August 1995 and it is assessed that the 1996 stock shortfall versus year earlier levels was considerably less at the end of August than at the end of July," the agency added.

The growth of North America's distillate inventories was unusually low in July and, at the end of the month, the year-on-year stock deficit hit 14 percent in North America, 10 percent in the Pacific, and four percent in Europe.
It was the first time OECD stocks have fallen in July since 1985, the IEA said.

The overall decline in OECD stocks in July was largely due to a 300,000 bpd fall in the Pacific, which was countered by a rise of 200,000 bpd in Europe. North American stocks fell by just 100,000 bpd.
